**Nomenclature:** ESC : Einstein summation convention.

## Problem 1 (15 pts) {-}

1. (10 pts)

    a. Not a vector space. Cannot add two elements to get an element in the same set. That is, $\pr{x_{1}, x_{2}, 2} + \pr{y_{1}, y_{2}, 2} = \pr{x_{1} + y_{1}, x_{2} + y_{2}, 4}$. But $\pr{x_{1} + y_{1}, x_{2} + y_{2}, 4}$ doesn't belong to the set.
    b. It is a 2D vector space, since it is a linear space (can add two elements to obtain an element in the same set, and multiply an element by a scalar to obtain an element in the same set) and it satisfies all the axioms of a vector space. $(1,0,0)$ and $(0,0,1)$ form a basis.
    c. It is a 4 dimensional vector space. Polynomials up to a finite degree satisfy the axioms of a vector space. The standard basis is $\cpr{1, x^1, x^2, x^3}$. Legendre polynomials up to the 3rd order also form a basis.
    d. It is a 2D vector space. In fact, $\mbb{C}$ is isomorphic to $\mbb{R}^2$, meaning there is a one to one map from elements of $\mbb{R}^2$ to $\mbb{C}$. The set $\cpr{1,i}$ forms a basis.
    e. Not a vector space. Matrix multiplication does not commute in general.

2. (5 pts) For the map to be linear, $T(u + v) = Tu + Tv$ and $T(\alpha u) = \alpha T u$, where $\alpha \in \mbb{R}$ and $u, v \in \mbb{R}^3$.
$$
\begin{aligned}
T(x_{1} + y_{1}, x_{2} + y_{2}, x_{3} + y_{3}) &= \pr{2 x_{1} + 2 y_{1} - 7 x_{2} - 7 y_{2} + x_{3} + y_{3} + b, 5 x_{1} + 5 y_{1} + c(x_{1}+y_{1})(x_{3}+y_{3})} \\
T(x_{1}, x_{2} ,x_{3}) + T(y_{1}, y_{2}, y_{3}) &= \pr{2 x_{1} + 2 y_{1} - 7 x_{2} - 7 y_{2} + x_{3} + y_{3} + b + b, 5 x_{1} + 5 y_{1} + c\, x_{1} x_{3} + c\, y_{1} y_{3}}
\end{aligned}
$$
The two are the same iff $b=0, c=0$.

## Problem 5 (20 pts) {-}

1.
$$
\begin{aligned}
(\bsf{u}\times\bsf{v})\cdot \bsf{w}+ (\bsf{w}\times\bsf{v})\cdot \bsf{u}&= \epsilon_{ijk}u_{j}v_{k} w_{i} + \epsilon_{ijk}w_{j}v_{k} u_{i} \\
&=\epsilon_{ijk}u_{j}v_{k} w_{i} +\epsilon_{ijk} w_{i}v_{j}u_{k}\\
&=\epsilon_{ijk}u_{j}v_{k} w_{i} +\epsilon_{ijk} v_{j}u_{k}w_{i}\\
&=\epsilon_{ijk}u_{j}v_{k} w_{i} -\epsilon_{ijk} u_{j}v_{k}w_{i}=0
\end{aligned}
$$

2.
$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{LHS:}\quad \det(\bsf{A}) &=\begin{vmatrix}
    A_{11}&A_{12}&A_{13}\\
    A_{21}&A_{22}&A_{23}\\
    A_{31}&A_{32}&A_{33}
    \end{vmatrix}\\
    &=A_{11}(A_{22}A_{33}-A_{23}A_{32})-A_{12}(A_{21}A_{33}-A_{31}A_{23})+A_{13}(A_{21}A_{32}-A_{31}A_{22})\\
    &=A_{11}A_{22}A_{33}+A_{31}A_{12}A_{23}+A_{21}A_{32}A_{13}-(A_{11}A_{32}A_{23}+A_{21}A_{12}A_{33}+A_{31}A_{22}A_{13})\\[1em]
\text{RHS:}\quad \epsilon_{ijk}A_{i1}A_{j2}A_{k3} &= A_{11}A_{22}A_{33}+A_{31}A_{12}A_{23}+A_{21}A_{32}A_{13}-(A_{11}A_{32}A_{23}+A_{21}A_{12}A_{33}+A_{31}A_{22}A_{13})
\end{aligned}
$$
Hence,
$$\det(\bsf{A})=\epsilon_{ijk}A_{i1}A_{j2}A_{k3}$$

3.
$$
\begin{aligned}
\bsf{a}\times(\bsf{b}\times\bsf{c}) &= \epsilon_{ijk}b_{j}c_{k}\epsilon_{mni}a_{n}\\
    &=\epsilon_{ijk}\epsilon_{imn}b_{j}c_{k}a_{n}\\
    &=(\delta_{jm}\delta_{kn}-\delta_{jn}\delta_{km})a_{n}b_{j}c_{k}\\
    &=\delta_{jm}\delta_{kn}a_{n}b_{j}c_{k}-\delta_{jn}\delta_{km}a_{n}b_{j}c_{k}\\
    &=a_{n}b_{m}c_{n}-a_{n}b_{n}c_{m}\\
    &=(\bsf{a}\cdot\bsf{c})\bsf{b}-(\bsf{a}\cdot\bsf{b})\bsf{c}
\end{aligned}
$$
